newsitem.title: CROATIA: Italy's ENEL interested in Croatian LNG terminal.
newsitem.headline: Italy's ENEL interested in Croatian LNG terminal.

text.p: Italy's power utility ENEL is looking to a Croatian project as an alternative terminal for liquified natural gas (LNG), Croatian oil firm INA Industrija Nafte said on Monday.

"They (ENEL) seem interested and there is very serious talk about it. We expect to hear from ENEL in about a month, month and a half," Mladen Sourek, project manager at INA's Naftaplin unit, told Reuters by telephone.
"If ENEL enters the project, building of the terminal could begin toward the end of 1997 for completion probably in 2001," he said of the $700 million Adriatic LNG project.

ENEL's interest in the Adriatic plan comes after it cancelled in December a long-term contract to buy LNG from a high-profile $4 billion Nigerian project and abandoned a projected gas plant north of Rome.
INA has some 20 percent in the multilateral project to build the LNG termninal and pipeline to central Europe that has been developed slowly for the past six years.
It is now in the final stage of intense preparations of technical and investment documentation, Sourek said.
To bring gas to the Italian side of the Adriatic, ENEL would have to build an underwater pipeline from the terminal, Sourek said but could not provide any cost figures or details.
He said France's Total SA joined other partners in the Malta-based Adria LNG Study company in 1991.
The project was planned to provide Croatia and neighbouring countries with 5.5-10 million cubic metres of natural gas which would be shipped to the island of Krk in northern Adriatic.
"This would not only be important for ensuring additional gas supplies to our economy, but would give it a different role in Europe," Sourek said.
He estimated the cost of a northbound pipeline at $270 million on top of the $700 million to build the terminal.
But a sluggish recovery of their post-communist economies has subdued the industrial demand for gas and in turn put the project's preparation on slow fire.

If and when ENEL joins, technical details would have to be wrapped up in the next few months and necessary funding found for the project to be launched later in the year, Sourek said. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
